name: Shobal
overview: Shobal was a male Edomite, known primarily as the son of Seir and a chief in Edom. His identity is grounded in his lineage and leadership within the Edomite tribe, reflecting his significance in the genealogical and tribal records of Genesis. There are no additional notes expanding on his character or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Shobal means "basket" in Hebrew, as recorded in Genesis 36:20. This is the only name associated with him, and it is a proper name not indicated as given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Shobal as the son of Seir. Additionally, inferred relationships suggest he was the father of Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam, indicating his role as a patriarch within his family line as detailed in Genesis 36:23.
scriptureSignificance: Shobal's significance lies in his position as a chief in Edom and as a descendant of Seir, marking him as an important figure in the genealogical structure of the Edomite people. His leadership role highlights the organization of the Edomite tribes and their chiefs, contributing to the biblical understanding of the peoples surrounding Israel. While not central to the broader biblical narrative, his mention preserves the historical and tribal context of Edom.
